name: EyeDropper
plain: Lets the person pick a colour from anywhere on screen.
meaning: Returns one pixel colour the person points at, including outside the page. Cannot capture other pixels.

access.prompt_ui: Magnifier cursor over the screen; Esc cancels
access.iframe: Same as top level; cross-origin iframes need a permissions policy where listed

edge.note: Before Edge 120, the EyeDropper API is not available on ChromeOS. See bug 40720753. Available on Linux X11, but not ava

data.metric: Lets the person pick a colour from anywhere on screen.

limits.headline: Can pick one color from anywhere on your screen when you click
limits.user_action: You tap Pick color and click a spot on the screen.
can: Show a magnifier so you can choose a color
Get the color code of the one spot you click
Work on any part of the screen, even outside the page
cannot: Take a screenshot or see anything but the color you click
Pick without you clicking; Esc cancels it
Keep picking after you click once
Work in Firefox, Safari, or on phones
limits.differs: Only desktop Chrome and Edge support it. Firefox, Safari and phone browsers do not.

story.what_it_is: A site can let you pick a colour from anywhere on your screen.

marketing.name: EyeDropper API
marketing.pitch: Chrome's blog says the API lets users sample a colour from anywhere on the screen.

story.for_you: You click a pipette tool and your cursor turns into a magnifier. You click and the page learns only that one colour.
story.for_makers: Makers can add a colour picker to design tools without extra apps. The page gets one value at a time and only after you click, so it cannot read your screen.

use_cases.example: A web design tool lets you grab a colour from a photo on another window.
A slide tool matches a chart colour to your logo.
A developer tool copies a colour from any site into code.
A makeup site lets you match a shade from a picture.
A drawing lesson lets kids sample colours from art.
A browser pixel art maker picks colours from a reference image.
